# Architecture Spine: Tamagai MVP

## Design Paradigm

**Hexagonal architecture (ports and adapters) around a deterministic engine core**, with unidirectional data flow (MVI) in the UI.
- The brain is an adapter that **proposes**. The safety engine and the engine form the core that **decides** (FR-43).
- Everything with I/O sits behind a port: microphone, camera, model runtimes, network, database, billing, clock.
- The server tier is a **stateless content pipeline** (talk gateway → recognizer → brain) beside a separate **records service**.

PRD and UX change requests raised by this architecture are in [CHANGE-REQUESTS.md](CHANGE-REQUESTS.md): ACR-A…ACR-Y for the PRD, UX-A…UX-M for UX. They were decided on 2026-10-03 ([outcome.md](discussion-change-decisions/outcome.md)); where an AD cites one, the AD follows the decided text. A request that waits on evidence carries an inline `[CONDITIONAL: request — trigger; fallback: what holds meanwhile]` tag at each dependent Rule (see the Assumption register).

# Tamagai MVP: architecture overview

The binding rules are the `AD-n` decisions in [ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md](ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md); if the two disagree, the spine wins. FR, NFR, CQ, OQ and CR-1…CR-10 are the PRD's IDs. ACR-A…ACR-Y and UX-A…UX-M are this architecture's change requests, in [CHANGE-REQUESTS.md](CHANGE-REQUESTS.md).

## 1. The shape in one paragraph

Tamagai is a native Android app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) built around a small, deterministic core. The **engine** decides what Pip does, and the **safety engine** checks every brain result first. The **brain** only proposes. It runs in one of two places, behind one interface and one reaction contract:
- **on the phone**, on capable phones: Gemma 4 E2B on LiteRT-LM;
- **on our own GPU server**, for every other device: Gemma 4 12B with the Qwen3-ASR recognizer on vLLM.

Pip's voice is always made on the phone. **Basic mode** needs no brain and no consent, and sends only the traffic FR-7.3 lists (ACR-A). The servers sit at a non-Google EU operator:
- **One GPU host** processes children's speech in memory only and makes no outbound internet calls.
- **A separate records host** keeps the few records the PRD allows: consent, linked parent, reports and counters. It never sees speech.

## 2. Context

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Child(["Child, 6–9"]) -- "taps, speech (talk only)" --> App["Tamagai app (Android)"]
  Parent(["Parent"]) -- "PIN, settings, purchase, consent screens" --> App
  Parent -- "email confirmation link, website" --> Records["Records service (our records host, EU)"]
  App -- "server tier only: voice turn" --> GPU["Talk gateway + brain (our GPU host, EU)"]
  App -- "config + link check, outbox, anonymous sends" --> Records
  App -- "model download (on-device tier)" --> Bucket["Object storage (EU)"]
  App -- "billing, age signal" --> Play["Google Play"]
  GPU -- "WireGuard: issuance checks" --> Records
  Records -- "purchase verification, voided purchases" --> Play
  Records -- "transactional email" --> Mail["Email provider (EU, named before family beta)"]
```

**Who processes what:**
- **Google** receives Play traffic and purchase data, never what the child says (PRD §9). The records service verifies a purchase with Google whenever the GPU host holds no valid binding for it (a memory-only link between the purchase and the consent receipt, kept 24 h at most), so at least daily per server-tier device. Google reports voided purchases through its Pub/Sub notification service.
- **Named processors** (addendum §2.2):
  - the hosting operator: GPU, records, backups and, by default, object storage;
  - the email provider;
  - a DNS provider, for certificates.

  All are covered by the CR-2 service-provider assurances.
- **The app** contains no third-party code with data access (NFR-11). It uses named libraries and the platform's own HTTPS client.
